claims.claim: On the Gemini API paid tier, Grounding with Google Search on Gemini 3.x models includes 5,000 free search requests a month shared across all Gemini 3.x models, then costs $14 per 1,000 requests.
On the Gemini API paid tier, Gemini 2.5 models get 1,500 grounded prompts a day free (Flash and Flash-Lite share one limit), then $35 per 1,000 grounded prompts.
On the Gemini API free tier, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Flash-Lite share 500 grounded requests a day, and Gemini 2.5 Pro gets no free grounding.

On Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Grounding with Google Search and Web Grounding for Enterprise on Gemini 3 include 5,000 grounding queries a month at no charge, aggregated across Gemini 3 models, then $14 per 1,000 queries, with each query charged.
Agent Platform billing for Gemini 3 grounding queries started on 2026-01-05.

On Agent Platform, Gemini 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Flash-Lite share 1,500 free grounding prompts a day and Gemini 2.5 Pro gets 10,000 a day; beyond that Google Search grounding costs $35 per 1,000 prompts, one charge per prompt however many queries it runs.
Web Grounding for Enterprise on Gemini 2.x models costs $45 per 1,000 grounding prompts on Agent Platform, with no free allowance listed.
Agent Platform asks customers to contact their account team above 1 million grounding prompts a day.
Agent Platform's Search-grounding documentation sets a limit of one million queries a day and says to contact support for more.
On Web Grounding for Enterprise, Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro Image are limited to 5,000 search queries a day.
Google bills Gemini 3 grounding per search query the model runs, so one prompt can create several charges, while Gemini 2.5 and older models are billed per grounded prompt.
Input tokens supplied by grounding are not charged: Agent Platform says so for Gemini 3 and the Gemini API says retrieved Search context is not billed as input tokens.
Google Search grounding and Web Grounding for Enterprise are billed only when a prompt returns at least one supporting web URL; Gemini model fees are charged separately.

On Gemini 3, Agent Platform lets customers skip displaying Search Suggestions at standard pricing below 1 million grounding prompts a day; on Gemini 2.0 Flash that waiver is subject to alternate pricing.
Agent Platform requires Search Suggestions to be enabled for Grounding with Google Search, and apps must display the suggestions they receive in production.

Web Grounding for Enterprise uses a subset of the Google Search index chosen for finance, healthcare and the public sector; fast-changing content refreshes every 6 hours and the whole index every 24 hours.
Web Grounding for Enterprise does not log or store customer data and supports VPC Service Controls (CMEK and Access Transparency don't apply).

Ordinary Grounding with Google Search keeps reliability logs for up to 3 days, and Google recommends it over Web Grounding for Enterprise for a broader, fresher index when the compliance controls aren't needed.
With Gemini 3, Google moved Search grounding from $35 per 1,000 grounded prompts (Gemini 2.x) to $14 per 1,000 search queries.
At launch in late 2024, Google Search grounding was free in AI Studio, unavailable on the free API tier, and $35 per 1,000 requests on the paid API tier.

Google documents Grounding with Parallel Web Search on Agent Platform as a Separate Offering bought through a Google Cloud Marketplace subscription or the customer's own Parallel key, with a zero-data-retention option.

Grounding with Google Web and Image Search on Gemini 3.x models is priced like text Search grounding: 5,000 free search requests a month shared across Gemini 3.x, then $14 per 1,000 (Gemini API row for text and image grounding; Agent Platform has a matching Web and Image Search line).
Google ignores empty web-search queries when counting billable Gemini 3 grounding queries.
On the Gemini API free tier, Grounding with Google Search is listed as not available for Gemini 3.x models, except the Gemini 3.8 Live models where it is marked supported.
A practitioner post reports 1 to 1.5 billed search queries per prompt in some optimized Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite grounded flows.
A Gemini API forum user reported in June 2026 that fewer than 500 Gemini 3 prompts produced more than 5,000 billed search requests, so the monthly allowance counts searches, not prompts.

A Gemini API forum moderator said in 2025 that Gemini 2.5 grounding overage is billed pro rata (10 prompts over the 1,500 free cost $0.35) and that each google_search call counts once however many queries it runs.

ModelsWar detected on 2026-07-21 that a Google Search grounding row reading 1,500 RPD free, then $35 per 1,000 grounded prompts was removed from the Gemini API pricing page (it doesn't say for which model).

A forum user reported on 2026-03-02 that the pricing page then listed, for gemini-3-flash-preview, 5,000 grounded requests a month on Standard and 1,500 a day on Batch, both at $14 per 1,000 searches (the current page shows 5,000 a month for Batch too).

questions.notes: Every price, allowance and limit the question asks for is pinned on Google's own pages (Gemini API pricing, updated 2026-09-24; Agent Platform pricing; WGE and Search-grounding docs, updated 2026-09-25), and the KB leaf already carries all of them. New: the Gemini 3 Web and Image Search grounding row ($14 per 1,000 after the shared 5,000), the empty-query billing rule, free-tier availability on Gemini 3, and practitioner and forum anecdotes on queries per prompt. The pricing page now says 5,000 free search requests; secondary pages (metacto, CloudZero, Puter, costgoat) still say prompts, and a forum user confirmed the allowance counts searches. Unsupported: c39 (the thread only asks the scope question; no answer); c59 (note.com doesn't say it, and Google's page shows free-tier grounding on Gemini 2.5 Flash, not on Gemini 3.x). ai.google.dev pages needed a cookie jar for curl; forum threads were read from their crawler view. c10, c26 and c51 are absence claims the WGE page is consistent with.

claims.claim: Alphabet reports Google Services, Google Cloud and Other Bets as its segments and discloses no standalone revenue for Gemini, the Gemini API or grounding; Google Cloud revenue bundles AI infrastructure, Vertex AI, Gemini Enterprise and other cloud services.
Alphabet said revenue from products built on its generative AI models grew more than 200% year over year in Q3 2025, without a dollar figure.
Alphabet said revenue from products built on its generative AI models grew nearly 400% year over year in Q4 2025, without a dollar figure.
Revenue from products built on Google's generative AI models grew nearly 800% in Q1 2026 (secondary reports of Alphabet's Q1 2026 results; no dollar figure).
Google Cloud revenue was $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, up 82% year over year.
Google Cloud revenue was $20 billion in Q1 2026, up 63% year over year.
Google Cloud ended 2025 at an annual revenue run-rate above $70 billion.
Google Cloud revenue was $13.6 billion in Q2 2025, up 32% year over year.
Google's first-party models such as Gemini processed 7 billion tokens a minute through direct customer API use in Q3 2025.
Google's first-party models such as Gemini processed over 10 billion tokens a minute through direct customer API use in Q4 2025.
Google's model APIs processed about 22 billion tokens a minute in Q2 2026, up from 16 billion a quarter earlier.
On the Gemini API paid tier, Grounding with Google Search on Gemini 3.x includes 5,000 free search requests a month shared across Gemini 3.x models, then costs $14 per 1,000 requests.
On Agent Platform, Gemini 3 grounding includes 5,000 search queries a month aggregated across Gemini 3 models, then costs $14 per 1,000 queries, each query charged, with billing from 2026-01-05.

On Agent Platform, Gemini 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Flash-Lite share 1,500 free grounding prompts a day and Gemini 2.5 Pro gets 10,000; beyond that Google Search grounding costs $35 per 1,000 prompts.
Web Grounding for Enterprise on Gemini 2.x models costs $45 per 1,000 grounding prompts on Agent Platform.
At launch on 2024-10-31, Grounding with Google Search on the Gemini API paid tier cost $35 per 1,000 grounded queries (Gemini 1.5 models) and was free to test in Google AI Studio.
Google bills Gemini 3 grounding per search query the model runs and Gemini 2.5 or older grounding per prompt.
Grounding is billed only when a prompt returns at least one supporting web URL, and Gemini model fees are charged separately.
Grounding with Google Search on Vertex AI (Agent Platform) has a documented limit of one million queries a day.
Apps must display the Google Search Suggestions returned with grounded results, and grounding skips pages whose publishers disallow Google-Extended.
Grounding with Google Search draws on Google's own search engine, which uses publicly available web data.
Alphabet said on its Q4 2025 call that Google Cloud's enterprise AI products were generating billions of dollars in quarterly revenue (no figure for Gemini API or grounding).
More than a dozen companies used Google's Vertex AI grounding service as of May 2025, according to court documents in the US search-remedies hearing; their names were redacted.

Google's head of search testified in May 2025 that companies paying for grounding via Vertex get the same web results as Gemini, but Gemini also gets extra search features such as the Knowledge Graph and OneBox.
The Information reported, per internal data, that Gemini API calls rose from about 35 billion in March 2025 to about 85 billion in August 2025 (relayed in a 2026-01-21 newsletter).
Nearly 350 Google Cloud customers each processed more than 100 billion tokens in December 2025.
Google Cloud revenue was $12.3 billion in Q1 2025, up 28% year over year.
Google Cloud revenue was $15.2 billion in Q3 2025, up 34% year over year.
Google Cloud revenue was $17.7 billion in Q4 2025, up 48% year over year.
Google Cloud's annual revenue run-rate was above $50 billion in Q2 2025.
In April 2026 a Google staff member acknowledged a bug that over-counted Gemini 3 search-grounding usage and said erroneous charges would be removed or refunded.
Sparkco projects a 2027 obtainable market of $1.2 billion ($0.6-2.8 billion) attributable to Gemini grounding features for Google Cloud; it is a speculative forecast with no traceable basis.

questions.notes: Unanswered. No pooled item shows Google disclosing, or anyone credibly reporting, grounding revenue or its share of Gemini API or Google Cloud AI revenue; Alphabet's closest disclosures are growth rates for gen-AI model products (200%, 400%, 800%) and 'billions in quarterly revenues' for enterprise AI products. The only grounding revenue figure in the pool is Sparkco's 2027 obtainable-market forecast, which is speculative and untraceable (usefulness 0). Best new context: court documents (May 2025) put Vertex grounding users at more than a dozen companies. Reuters (c9, c13, c18) returned 401 live and in its only Wayback capture: unverifiable. SEC exhibits and abc.xyz calls were read on Wayback. Irrelevant: c22 (Vertex model catalogue), c36 (Gemini enterprise adoption and names), c49 (Cloud customers not tied to grounding; the transcript says Loews, not Lowe's). aibusinessweekly dates the 85 billion API requests to January 2026; The Information's figure is August 2025, so it isn't counted as support.

claims.claim: Value Add VC's revenue page (updated September 2026) splits OpenAI's roughly $40 billion August 2026 run-rate into about $22 billion from ChatGPT subscriptions, about $12 billion from API consumption and about $6 billion from Sora, ads and licensing; it is an estimate, not an OpenAI disclosure.

Value Add VC's product-line table puts OpenAI's API (GPT-5-class models) at a $6.5 billion run-rate for February to June 2026, 26% of a $25.0 billion total, after $8.0 billion at the end of 2025 and $0.8 billion in 2024.
An earlier version of the same Value Add VC page (last updated 2026-09-03) said about 25% of OpenAI's revenue is API consumption, next to roughly 70% from ChatGPT subscriptions.

Value Add VC's June 2026 enterprise analysis put OpenAI's API platform at about $3-4 billion of a $20 billion-plus run-rate, of which about $1.2-1.5 billion was consumption by large enterprise accounts, separate from Microsoft licensing.
SecondTalent's ChatGPT statistics page says about a quarter of OpenAI's roughly $25 billion (February 2026) revenue mix comes from API usage.
Searchlab estimates OpenAI's 2026 API revenue at about $3.2 billion, about 25% of the $12.7 billion Q1 2026 run-rate it reports.
Thrad estimates OpenAI's API revenue at a $2.8-3.2 billion annualized run-rate in Q1 2026.
Meridian48 projects OpenAI's 2026 API (developer and business) revenue at $3.5 billion, up from $1.6 billion in 2025, on a $20.0 billion total.
FutureSearch estimated OpenAI's API revenue at a $510 million annualized rate as of 2024-06-12.
Sacra estimates that OpenAI's API and licensing (model-as-a-service) business contributes 15-20% of its total revenue.
OpenAI's annualized revenue run-rate reached about $40 billion by July-August 2026.
OpenAI said on 2026-03-31 that it was generating $2 billion in revenue a month.
OpenAI's annualized revenue run-rate topped $25 billion by February 2026.
OpenAI's revenue run-rate cleared $13 billion annualized in April 2026.
OpenAI said in March and April 2026 that enterprise made up more than 40% of its revenue and was on track to reach parity with consumer by the end of 2026.
OpenAI's CFO told investors in August 2026 that enterprise revenue now exceeds consumer, after OpenAI entered 2026 at a 60-40 consumer-enterprise split.
OpenAI's CFO put company ARR at $2 billion in 2023, $6 billion in 2024 and more than $20 billion in 2025.
OpenAI's APIs processed more than 15 billion tokens a minute as of March-April 2026.
About 4 million developers build on OpenAI's platform.
OpenAI describes its usage-based APIs separately from consumer and workplace subscriptions but discloses no standalone API revenue figure.
OpenAI's recognized revenue was $5.7 billion in Q1 2026 and $6.7 billion in Q2 2026.
OpenAI disclosed that more than 9,000 organizations have processed over 10 billion tokens through its API and nearly 200 have exceeded 1 trillion tokens each.
OpenAI said in November 2025 that more than 1 million business customers pay it directly, through ChatGPT for Work or direct model consumption on its developer platform.
Sacra says its OpenAI annualized revenue figures exclude Microsoft licensing revenue and large one-time deals, and that Microsoft retains resell rights through 2032.
On 2026-07-30 OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna's API price 80% (to $0.20 input and $1.20 output per million tokens) and GPT-5.6 Terra's 20% (to $2 and $12).
Since 2026-05-19 OpenAI has sold 1-, 2- and 3-year compute commitments with discounts that rise with commitment size.
OpenAI's run-rate rose about 20% month over month in July 2026.
OpenAI's ChatGPT ads business reached about a $1 billion annualized run-rate by August 2026.
Sacra describes OpenAI's API as usage-priced and powering third-party apps such as Notion, Salesforce and Bing, with Microsoft's payments for API usage entangled with its investment deal.

questions.notes: Partial. OpenAI discloses no API revenue; the pool offers only third-party estimates, and they disagree by about 4x: roughly $3 billion at Q1 2026 (Thrad, Searchlab), $3-4 billion (Value Add VC, June), $6.5 billion or 26% (Value Add VC's February-June table), 15-20% (Sacra; about $6-8 billion on a $40 billion run-rate) and about $12 billion (Value Add VC's August split, repeated by AInvest). The KB's $4B / $6B / $8B sits inside that spread; the $12 billion estimate is the only one above its high case, and Value Add VC's own pages contradict each other. Searchlab's $12.7 billion Q1 2026 base conflicts with OpenAI's own $2 billion a month, and Meridian48's $11.2 billion for 2025 conflicts with the $13.07 billion in the KB. Value Add VC merged its 25B-ARR posts into one URL (c11, c42, r17 and r28 now redirect there); c11 and c16's 25% share was read on a Wayback capture from 2026-09-14. The live page now says $12 billion. Unverifiable: Reuters (c2, c30, c35, c49, c54; 401 live and on Wayback) and Bloomberg (c13; 403). Irrelevant: named customers (c3, c24, c57), compute suppliers (c28), the Fortune 500 adoption share (c51). False: CallSphere's $13 billion April 2026 run-rate (r16).
